narrative.overview: This is the second visual world for Elite Legacy, replacing an engraved-certificate identity with one pinned directly by the user from two reference images. The old certificate world is retired entirely — this world proves trust through a real family's face, not an institution's seal. The system is built on a single real photograph doing the emotional work in the hero, a warm neutral cream base for reading sections, and deep forest-black for alternating dark sections and the footer. Sage green is the one working accent.
keyCharacteristics: Real, diverse family photography carries warmth — a full-bleed hero photo plus a supporting gallery
Manrope for nearly everything, with Source Serif 4 italic reserved for a single warm emphasis word per headline
Soft, fully-rounded pill buttons and 2xl-rounded cards throughout
Alternating cream / forest section grounds, sage green as the sole accent color
Diverse representation is deliberate: the hero leads with a Black family; the supporting gallery spans other families and generations

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Sage is the only accent color in the system.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: Source Serif italic appears at most once per headline, on the single word or phrase carrying the emotional turn.

rules.name: The No-Border Rule
rules.body: Cards separate from their ground with shadow and fill contrast only, never a stroke.

dos: Do keep sage as the only accent color.
Do use fully-rounded pills for every button and rounded-2xl for every card.
Do build any photo overlay gradient from the forest hex at varying alpha.
Do alternate cream and forest section grounds for rhythm.
Do keep the Source Serif italic accent to one short phrase per headline.
donts: Don't reintroduce the retired certificate-world elements: ribbon buttons, engraved seals, brass ornament, roman numerals, underline-only inputs.
Don't put a border/stroke on a card.
Don't introduce a second accent color alongside sage.
Don't caption real family photography with a name or quote implying a specific endorsement.
